A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same DiffStateGrad research work and complete appendices A-E. Full-text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the methods, equations, results, and presentation.

before.justification: v3 reports original DiffStateGrad image-restoration experiments in Section 4 and Appendices A-B, plus an original MRI evaluation in Appendix E.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experiments, including FFHQ/ImageNet comparisons and the 30-example fastMRI evaluation in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The SVD-based adaptive gradient projection, Algorithms 1-5, and solver-specific and MRI integrations are unchanged. The appendix edits clarify baseline reproduction without modifying algorithmic steps.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same linear and nonlinear restoration tasks on FFHQ and ImageNet and accelerated MRI on T2-weighted fastMRI brain data. The noise, step-size, and reconstruction-diversity scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership within corresponding experiments is unchanged: PSLD, ReSample, DPS, DAPS, DDNM, DDRM, MCG, and MPGD-AE retain their respective comparisons, as does CSGM-Langevin in Appendix E.

E3.justification: The samples, preprocessing, pretrained models, metrics, and testing procedures remain unchanged. Appendix C.3-C.6 clarifies that default configurations are used for reproducing baselines; it reports no revised parameter values or evaluation design.

E4.justification: Both retain the subspace comparison, failure-rate analysis, step-size and noise robustness tests, rank and projection-period sensitivity analyses, and qualitative and diversity examples, including the MRI robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Mean/standard-deviation reporting and plotted uncertainty are unchanged, including Appendix E's averaging over 30 test examples. v5 introduces no additional run-count, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing information.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plotted findings, and qualitative examples are retained. For example, Table 3 reports the same phase-retrieval PSNR values for ReSample, 27.61 (8.07), and DiffStateGrad-ReSample, 31.19 (4.33), in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, projection equations, Proposition 1, and Appendix D proof are unchanged, including the tangent-space approximation and small-step-size assumptions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about manifold preservation, robustness, worst-case reliability, and improved inverse-problem reconstruction across diffusion solvers.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and result interpretations are unchanged. Both retain the learned-prior reliability and bias limitations, the black-hole-imaging caution in Section 5, and the preliminary, small-sample qualification for MRI in Appendix E.

D1.justification: The abstract and Section 6 update the code-access target from neuraloperator/DiffStateGrad to Anima-Lab/DiffStateGrad. Appendix C.3-C.6 expands the default-configuration statements to explicitly mention noise, step size, and baseline reproduction, without supplying new numerical settings.

R1.justification: The cited works and reference list are unchanged, as are the comparisons with prior manifold-projection approaches and the positioning of DiffStateGrad's contribution.

P1.justification: v5 adds Section 7 with funding acknowledgments and author responsibilities and expands four configuration sentences in Appendix C.3-C.6. The existing scientific narrative and section organization are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: The abstract reflows after the repository-link update, and acknowledgments occupy previously blank space on page 11. Figures 1-17, Tables 1-6, and algorithm displays retain their content, structure, and placement.

improvement.justification: v5 modestly improves reporting through clearer baseline-reproduction statements in Appendix C.3-C.6 and explicit funding and author-contribution disclosures in Section 7. These provide limited transparency gains; the scientific method, evidence, and limitations remain unchanged.
